analyst.summary: Bajaj Housing Finance remains a best-in-class prime housing lender on credit quality (GNPA ~0.27-0.30%, NNPA ~0.11%, credit cost ~0.19%) with AUM reaccelerating to +24% YoY (Rs 1,49,610cr, Q1 FY27) -- the franchise itself shows no sign of the deterioration the quant model's '3-year de-rating momentum' Sell might imply if read literally as a fundamentals signal. What it does correctly capture is a real, ongoing valuation-vs-returns tension: at ~3.2x book for a 12.1% ROE that is still running below the company's own 13-15% medium-term guidance six-plus quarters after listing, with NIM actively compressing (4.0% to 3.8% Q3-to-Q4 FY26) on bank/PSB prime-mortgage competition, the stock is priced meaningfully richer than peers (LIC Housing Finance 12.36% ROE at 0.78x book; PNB Housing 12.27% ROE at 1.25-1.42x book) delivering comparable-or-better current returns. Roughly 38% of the post-IPO multiple excess has already unwound (5.2x to ~3.2x book), and sell-side is split (JPMorgan Underweight/Rs 70 target vs Morgan Stanley constructive) on whether that is enough. Net call: Hold the existing position on the strength of asset quality and reaccelerating growth, but this is a genuine, non-trivial judgment call given the unresolved ROE-vs-peer valuation gap -- escalating for principal visibility rather than presenting false precision.
